reading.body:
Capitol Counsel's AI lobbying book is led by an electric utility trade group, not a technology company. The Edison Electric Institute accounts for 10 of the firm's 32 AI filings, more than any other client.

The client list splits between health care and software. The Healthcare Leadership Council and Baxter Healthcare together account for 9 filings, and Intuit accounts for 2. The remaining named clients are Covestro, a chemicals manufacturer, and the utility group. That mix suggests AI lobbying here is mostly about how AI rules land on regulated industries rather than about AI products themselves.

The work is spread across many lobbyists rather than concentrated. Shannon Finley appears on 17 filings, Jeffrey Carroll on 13, and Joseph Eannello and David Olander on 12 each, with 20 more names below them. Six bills are named in filings from 2025 or later, four in the Senate and two in the House.

The data covers only what the firm reported under the Lobbying Disclosure Act. It records that a client lobbied on an issue, not what position it took, so nothing here shows whether these clients supported or opposed any AI measure. It also gives no dollar amounts, no committee or agency targets, and no indication of whether the filings concern federal AI legislation, agency rulemaking, or both.

summary: CAPITOL COUNSEL LLC filed 22 Lobbying Disclosure Act reports on AI held by this site. Its clients, the lobbyists named on those filings and the AI bills they name are below. LDA registrant id 313715.
